The test image shows a young corn plant with striking **excessive tillering** — multiple shoots/side stems emerging from a single base at soil level, creating a bushy multi-stemmed appearance. The plant is noticeably smaller/younger than the tall corn in the background.

The Crazy_top reference collage shows exactly this pattern: proliferative tillering with numerous side shoots erupting from the base, identical bushy multi-stemmed growth habit. This is the hallmark symptom of Crazy top (caused by *Sclerophthora macrospora*), which triggers excessive vegetative proliferation and tillering in infected plants.
